### Prospective deployment of multimodal AI grading for medical student OSCEs

- **Auteurs** : Huong-Tra Ngo, Ameer Hamza Shakur, Michael J. Holcomb, Shinyoung Kang, David Hein, Judah K Gruen, Hunter Schuler, Philip C. Jarrett, Thomas O. Dalton, Krystle K. Campbell, Daniel Scott, Andrew Raymond Jamieson

- **Tags proposés** : `#education_medicale`, `#sciences_education`

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **education_anchor** : medical education, undergraduate medical education
  - **osce_ecos** : OSCE, OSCEs, objective structured clinical examinations
  - **competency_assessment** : clinical competence
  - **ai_anchor** : artificial intelligence

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) are central to assessing medical student clinical competence, but human grading imposes substantial burden. We report, to our knowledge, the first prospective deployment of an integrated multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) system for OSCE grading in undergraduate medical education, spanning notes, audio, and video. We present MAPLES (Multimodal Assessment Pipeline for Learning Encounter Scoring), a rubric-driven zero-shot system deployed in Fall 2025 for 222 students (72,907 retained item-level scores). In the routed low-scoring review set, tolerant AI–SPE agreement was 85.7–92.4% by modality. In a selected, non-blinded set of 616 adjudicated disagreements, physician scores matched AI on 76.0% of items and the SPE on 19.0%. Human scoring passes fell by 92.3% versus a modeled single-pass manual comparator. Together, these findings show that multimodal AI first-pass scoring can be embedded in routine OSCE operations, with human review on the low-scoring tail and physician adjudication of selected disagreements.

Metode: Penelitian kuantitatif observasional analitik pendekatan cross-sectional dilakukan pada mahasiswa angkatan 2024 Fakultas Kedokteran Universitas Muhammadiyah Semarang menggunakan teknik total sampling. Kesimpulan: Semakin tinggi emotional intelligence, semakin rendah academic anxiety mahasiswa dalam menghadapi ujian OSCE.

> Medical education increasingly adopts problem-based learning (PBL) to foster clinical reasoning; however, its impact on student mental health remains unclear. A significant knowledge gap persists regarding whether PBL acts as a protective factor or a risk intensifier for burnout, as current evidence is fragmented and heterogeneous. This systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence to inform curricular decisions following PRISMA guidelines. Eight studies (n = 1,203) were analyzed, with quality assessed via JBI and CASPe tools. Findings reveal a weighted mean burnout prevalence of 31.8%, primarily linked to systemic stressors such as sleep deprivation rather than the curricular model itself. While most studies found no global difference in burnout prevalence between PBL and traditional models, high-rigor research associates PBL with lower emotional exhaustion and higher professional efficacy. PBL is not a universal protective factor against burnout, as the syndrome is driven by the inherent rigors of medical training regardless of methodology. **Résumé / abstract :**

> This scoping review maps generative AI applications in workplace-based assessment (WBA) and analyzes validity evidence through Downing’s framework. Following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, four databases were searched (2022-February 2026) with dual-AI screening and human adjudication. Data were mapped to Downing’s five validity sources using AI-assisted extraction with human verification. Thirteen studies (2024–2025) met inclusion criteria. All AI applications operated on pre-existing text; feedback analysis predominated (9/13). Content (12/13), Response Process (13/13), and Relationship to Other Variables (12/13) were well addressed, while Internal Structure (2/13) and Consequences (4/13) were neglected. AI reasoning transparency, inter-model agreement, and internal consistency were absent (0/13). Current evidence concentrates on AI-human agreement, neglecting reproducibility, bias testing, and learner impact evidence essential for responsible deployment. Realising AI’s potential to reduce faculty burden will require non-supervisor oversight mechanisms for continuous validity monitoring, particularly for direct learner-facing applications.

> Background The growing adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly ChatGPT, has created new opportunities for medical education by supporting learning, problem-solving, and knowledge acquisition. However, evidence regarding the psychological and individual factors influencing ChatGPT adoption among medical students remains limited. This study develops and tests an integrated theoretical model that combines Privacy Theory, Technostress Theory, Affect Theory, Diffusion of Innovation Theory, and the Theory of Planned Behavior to explain ChatGPT adoption. BENCH, PrIME-LLM and PatientSafeBench); and general LLM reasoning evaluation research, including the Factuality-Validity-Coherence-Utility taxonomy, FaithCoT-Bench and C2-Faith. > Background: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) comprise conditions affecting the temporomandibular joints, masticatory muscles, and associated structures. Conservative management commonly includes education, self-management, therapeutic exercise, and selected manual interventions. Osteopathic techniques are sometimes incorporated into rehabilitation, although their additional benefit within multimodal programmes remains uncertain. Objective: To describe a structured clinical pathway integrating orthopaedic manual therapy, selected osteopathic techniques, and physiotherapy for patients with TMD in an outpatient rehabilitation setting. > We report two cases of Bordetella bronchiseptica isolation from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in patients with pre-existing lung conditions. Case 1 describes a 75-year-old male with COPD, organizing pneumonia on high-dose steroids, and presenting hemoptysis with acute pulmonary consolidations on CT, who was successfully treated with targeted antibiotics. Case 2 describes a 71-year-old female with long-standing bronchiectasis and prior non-tuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) disease presenting with a persistent dry cough and new tree-in-bud opacities, managed conservatively without antimicrobial therapy. Specific interpretive breakpoints for clinical decision-making concerning the isolation of B. bronchiseptica are lacking; therefore, management remains challenging.

> PURPOSE: Forward head posture (FHP) is commonly assessed using isolated cervical measures, potentially overlooking its relationship with global sagittal alignment. This study introduces the Global Sagittal Deviation Index (GSDI-5), a composite measure integrating multiregional sagittal alignment with explicit inclusion of the upper cervical spine. METHODS: Standing lateral EOS radiographs from 201 adults referred for evaluation of low back pain were analysed and classified into FHP and non-FHP groups. Standardized sagittal parameters across the cervical, thoracic, lumbar, and global spine were combined into a single score. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Fairness metric selection is typically left to data scientists, but which biases are problematic and which metric captures them best depends on stakeholders' experience and domain knowledge. This calls for involving non-technical stakeholders, but the research prototypes built for this purpose so far have not tested whether these stakeholders form accurate mental models of the metrics they interact with or can act on them to identify biases. We present FairAware, a fairness assessment tool co-designed with Human Resources (HR) domain experts. We evaluate stakeholders' understanding through a mixed-methods study with 70 participants (35 HR employees, 35 job seekers), measuring objective and subjective understanding, cognitive load, bias identification accuracy, and open-ended feedback. Most participants correctly identified the most disadvantaged group, with task duration being the only significant predictor. We also found a gap between subjective and objective understanding, with both groups performing similarly across all measures. These results suggest that fairness assessment tools for non-experts are usable for identifying biases but need built-in checks on understanding before...

> Chemistry, environmental health, and occupational health have historically developed in close collaboration. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of LLMs, in responding to a chemistry course questionnaire used in environmental and occupational health department for educational purposes. This was a cross-sectional study conducted in 2026. The study used a 50-item multiple-choice questionnaire, primarily in Persian with limited English terms and formulas, which was administered to LLMs (ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini 3, and Copilot 2026). Performance was evaluated using confusion matrix analysis. Cochran`s Q test, McNemar`s test for pair-wise comparisons, and Point-biserial correlation were also conducted to further evaluate the study data. The LLMs presented mean sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 0.81, 0.29, and 0.68, respectively. Gemini 3 presented a high level of performance, achieving the highest sensitivity (0.85), specificity (0.56), and accuracy (0.80). ChatGPT-5.5 had the lowest sensitivity (0.76), while Copilot showed the lowest specificity (0.07) and an accuracy of 0.62. > Since time immemorial, different cultures have utilized the extracts of plants to improve the rheological behavior of primitive mortars and concretes, with prickly pear mucilage serving as one of the best examples of traditional construction. In this research, the main aim is to analyze how Opuntia ficus-indica mucilage, a plentiful natural material in the region of Huancayo in Peru, influences the properties of structural concrete as a plasticizing and densifying additive. To achieve this, experiments on how the additive works in mixtures having a specified resistance to compression of f’c = 280 kg/cm² using local aggregates were carried out. The workability of the concrete was assessed by a slump test, while the compressive strength was assessed at 7, 14 and 28 days. The penetration test method was used to find the setting time, and the method of measuring the porous phase was done through gravimetric methods. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Long COVID is a multi-system, heterogeneous condition that manifests as new or worsened symptoms lasting at least 3 months following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, often despite normal results on routine diagnostic testing. Common manifestations include fatigue, post-exertional malaise, cognitive impairment, and orthostatic intolerance. Primary care clinicians are uniquely positioned to identify and manage Long COVID due to their longitudinal relationships with patients and holistic understanding of their patients' health. However, diagnostic uncertainty, time constraints, and limited access to specialty care present significant challenges, and sometimes hesitation, to addressing Long COVID in the primary care setting. This focused narrative review provides a pragmatic, primary care-focused approach for the evaluation and management of Long COVID. Using patient-centered vignettes, we first describe common clinical presentations. Next, we provide a framework for the pathophysiological mechanisms suspected to contribute to persistent symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection. We then present a simple approach to Long COVID diagnosis and management that leverages primary care clinicians' skill...

- **Source** : OpenAlex

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **education_anchor** : health professions education

**Résumé / abstract :**

> ABSTRACT Uncertainty is a precursor to learning. Learning in today's complex and rapidly changing world requires a simple and adaptive approach that works. One that is based in inquiry and has deep underlying theoretical roots. Adaptive Action is such an approach. It consists of three simple questions: What? So What? and Now What? It is what we do naturally when dealing with uncertainty. The education of future health professionals is used as an example and a context for the application of Adaptive Action. The CDE model is presented as the underlying theory of Adaptive Action. Adaptive Action, while presented in the context of the education and practice of health professionals, is a universal method to deal with uncertainty at multiple levels.

> Contemporary interest in glocalisation partly reflects the limitations of earlier globalising movements in medical education. The former evolves to a process through which globally-informed educational models are negotiated and reconstituted within local contexts. While global standards can enhance graduate mobility, implementation may privilege Western assumptions regarding competence, professionalism, and quality. This can lead to obscuration of local values, needs and realities. Existing scholarship has examined glocalisation through sociocultural and postcolonial perspectives, generating insights into issues of hierarchy, power, and culture. Less explored is how methodology can empower transferable explanations of how global educational interventions generate different outcomes across contexts. We argue glocalisation can be considered a wicked problem: a complex, context-dependent phenomenon shaped by interacting pedagogical, regulatory, and socio-political forces. > This study examines the long-term career outcomes of medical graduates who served as tutors in a Peer-Assisted Learning (PAL) program. Using a descriptive phenomenological approach, semi-structured interviews with fifteen graduates explored how PAL influenced teaching competence, motivation, and professional identity. Guided by Self-Determination Theory and Kirkpatrick’s framework, findings indicate that PAL functioned as an early catalyst for interest in medical education, provided a safe environment to develop teaching skills, and supported the formation of an educator identity. Skills acquired through PAL were transferable to clinical practice, fostering sustained engagement in educational roles and supporting the development of future clinician educators.

> The war has substantially changed the conditions under which higher medical education institutions in Ukraine operate. It has had a significant impact on institutional functioning, the educational process, and students’ future careers, while also creating numerous challenges and limitations for educational institutions, students, and teaching staff. Wartime conditions require flexibility, creativity, and cooperation among all stakeholders to ensure safety and continuity of the educational process. Distance learning, which was widely implemented and tested during the COVID-19-related quarantine restrictions, has become one of the principal forms of education for students in both secondary and higher education. However, distance learning under wartime conditions differs fundamentally from that experienced during the quarantine period. It provides opportunities to stay connected, communicate, collaborate, continue learning, and maintain a sense of purpose despite challenging circumstances. Distance-learning platforms are effective educational tools that help diversify the learning process and support students’ development.

> Artificial intelligence (AI) can reproduce and amplify the structural inequities faced by minoritized communities. Participatory AI has been proposed as a response, but participation typically starts after problem definitions and success criteria have been set, leaving limited room for minoritized communities to reshape what an AI system is for. We propose AI From the Margins (AIM): a methodological stance that articulates the conditions under which lived experiences of minoritized communities can be elicited, centered, and carried forward to inform participatory AI design. AIM is not a fixed protocol; it articulates a set of preconditions that can be enacted through different techniques in different settings. We applied AIM in a Dutch healthcare context in eight sessions with 13 women and non-binary people of color and five municipal policy workers, namely through (1) narrative elicitation using the Biographic Narrative Interpretive Method (BNIM); (2) co-constructed rule-making; (3) participants' determination of whether, where, and how AI should be involved; and (4) translating lived experience into AI policy through dialogue with policymakers. > As large language models (LLMs) enter high-stakes domains such as healthcare, understanding their moral reasoning becomes essential. Decisions about scarce medical resources often hinge on judgments of responsibility, particularly when patients' own actions contribute to illness. We investigate how LLMs reason about responsibility and its consequences, tracing their judgments across successive levels, from the behavior, to the resulting illness, to the denial of care. We evaluate a wide range of LLMs, spanning different model families and capability levels, on various clinical vignettes adapted from prior studies. Our results identify a judgment-consequence gap: LLMs largely agree with humans that patients bear responsibility for health-harming behaviors, yet overwhelmingly refuse to let that judgment influence how they allocate scarce resources. Specifically, LLMs default to random allocation, whereas humans consistently favor the less-culpable patient. > In a two-year action-research study within an undergraduate biostatistics curriculum for nursing, pharmacy, and medical biotechnology students, we examined how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) facilitates educators to design, supervise, and evaluate learning. Students used GenAI first as a technical tutor and then as a partner in knowledge co-creation in case-based statistical problem-solving. Teachers’ reflection records and 4697 LINE messages during the study period were analyzed using qualitative coding, GenAI-assisted semantic analysis, and social network analysis. Teachers’ roles shifted from knowledge transmitters to facilitators of critical inquiry and human–GenAI co-learning. Overall, faculty communication was dense, reciprocal, and decentralized, whereas GenAI-related discourse was more selective and centralized. GenAI-related ties were less likely to form but, once formed, strongly reciprocal and locally clustered. GenAI integration can catalyze new forms of faculty leadership through expertise sharing and collaborative problem-solving. Intentional structures for cross-disciplinary exchange and reflective faculty development are needed.

In East Asia, where obesity is less prevalent than in Western countries, the relative contribution of these different drivers may differ, underscoring the need for region-specific phenotypic characterization.   - **ai_anchor** : large language models

**Résumé / abstract :**

> This chapter explores the ergonomic, cognitive, and psychological mechanisms underpinning human–robot communication, focusing on the role of social robots in shaping human perception, behaviour, and socio-emotional engagement. By analysing factors such as robot design, embodiment, and communication modalities, the chapter highlights how these elements influence user interaction and the perception of robots as social entities. It examines the integration of verbal and non-verbal communication modalities, addressing challenges in reciprocity and robots’ behavioural appropriateness. The discussion extends to the implications of adaptive technologies like large language models, emphasising the balance between responsiveness and confidentiality in human–robot interactions. Furthermore, the chapter underscores the potential of social robots in workplace and therapeutic settings to enhance efficiency, safety, and emotional well-being of human interactants. By addressing user expectations and ethical considerations, the chapter seeks to provide a comprehensive framework for advancing social robotics applications in fostering meaningful human–robot relationships.

Knowledge and understanding of patterns and the factors sustaining them is essential for creating effective, developmentally informed prevention and intervention responses to reduce the incidence and impact of IPV. This scoping review examined literature on patterns of IPV and general antisociality by individuals who perpetrate IPV across adolescence and adulthood, and summarised factors linked to varying levels of IPV or subgroup membership. Sixty-three studies were included, primarily spanning adolescence (12–18 years) or early adulthood (up to mid-30s). Findings indicate most individuals do not engage in long-term IPV, with physical and sexual violence peaking around mid-adolescence (age 16–17) and generally declining thereafter. > Online Qur’anic instruction is often discussed as a problem of access, platforms, or learner outcomes, while the lived work of women who teach recitation through screens remains comparatively underexamined. This qualitative phenomenological study explores how four Indonesian female tutors at a non-formal Qur’anic education provider experienced the transition to and practice of online teaching. Data were generated through semistructured interviews and analyzed through descriptive phenomenological procedures, including bracketing, repeated reading, meaning-unit condensation, thematic synthesis, and cross-case comparison. Cyberfeminism was used after inductive analysis as an interpretive lens for examining women’s participation in digitally mediated religious knowledge production. Three interdependent themes were identified. First, tutors reconstructed embodied Qur’anic pedagogy under conditions of sensory attenuation by intensifying listening, slowing and repeating recitation, externalizing articulation through images and video, differentiating correction, and cultivating relational presence. > Abstract Problematic Internet Use (PIU) is associated with difficulties in psychological, social, academic, and occupational functioning and is associated with unhealthy behaviours such as poor diet, inactivity, and sleep problems. The post-pandemic period has intensified PIU and Internet addiction, especially among young men, who are more prone to risky health behaviours. This study aimed to assess the relationship between health behaviours, PIU, and serotonin and dopamine levels in young men. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 325 men aged 18–30 from the West Pomeranian region of Poland. PIU severity was measured using the Internet Use Test (IUT), and health behaviours were assessed using the Health-Related Behaviour Inventory (HBI). Blood samples were analysed for serotonin and dopamine levels using ELISA. 17.7% of participants exhibited high or very high PIU. One-third led unhealthy lifestyles. **Résumé / abstract :**

> BACKGROUND: Warm-up is a central preparatory phase of training and competition, aimed at optimizing physiological and neuromuscular readiness for subsequent performance and reducing the risk of injury. However, the athlete warm-up literature spans diverse sports, populations, and intervention models, with substantial variability in protocol content, outcome selection, and reporting. No prior scoping review with an Evidence Gap Map (EGM) has comprehensively mapped this evidence across sports, warm-up modalities, and outcome domains. OBJECTIVES: To map the landscape of warm-up evidence in athletes, identify the main intervention types and outcome domains investigated, and locate key evidence gaps related to methodology, population coverage, sport specificity, and real-world applicability. METHODS: A scoping review with EGM was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidance, with methodological considerations informed by the PRISMA 2020 statement. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, SPORTDiscus, and Web of Science Core Collection for studies published up to 20th January 2026. Eligible studies examined warm-up practices in athletes across competitive sports and evaluated perfo...

> Crowned dens syndrome (CDS) is a rare crystal deposition disorder characterized by distinctive halo-like or coronal calcification surrounding the odontoid process, primarily manifesting as neck pain and restricted mobility, occasionally accompanied by systemic inflammatory signs.The present report describes two cases of patients with this condition with the aim of elucidating the clinical spectrum and management of CDS.The first case involved a 72-year-old male patient who exhibited marked symptom relief following treatment with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and a brief corticosteroid regimen, with no recurrence noted over a 2-year follow-up period.The second case involved an 81-year-old male patient who developed severe cervical spinal cord compression due to a calcified pseudotumor posterior to the odontoid process, leading to debilitating neurological deficits.This patient underwent a posterior atlas arch resection with microscopy assistance, resulting in the marked alleviation of spinal cord compression symptoms and sustained improvement over 3 years of follow-up.On the whole, the present report underscores the importance of recognizing CDS and highlights that isolated...

> The increasing deployment of autonomous, agentic AI systems challenges traditional accountability mechanisms. Existing research predominantly frames AI accountability gaps as barriers that can be overcome through better standards, transparency, and institutional reform. We argue that this framing is insufficient: certain configurations of actors, systems, and institutions render AI accountability conceptually unachievable regardless of effort. We introduce the concept of constitutive AI unaccountability to capture these configurations. Through a three-stage qualitative study comprising a concept-centric literature analysis, a secondary analysis of 27 expert interviews with AI professionals from technical, legal, and sociotechnical backgrounds, and an illustrative framework application to the open-source agentic AI system OpenClaw, we identify nine categories and 20 themes of constitutive AI unaccountability. These are organized across structural, technological, and normative clusters and reinforce one another through eight directed interdependencies. ### Bilateral upper‐limb palsy of the newborn infant: Taxonomy, differential diagnosis, and clinical pathways

- **Auteurs** : Yegee Han, Yangmyung Ma, Kanwal Yousaf, Evangeline Wassmer, Andrea Jester

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **spine_reasoning_triage** : differential diagnosis
  - **low_priority_clinical_topics** : neurology

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Bilateral reduction or absence of upper-limb movement in a newborn infant is a rare but critical presentation that cannot be anchored on the unilateral paradigm of brachial plexus birth injury (BPBI). Bilaterality substantially widens the differential to include cervical spinal cord injury, neuromuscular disorders, and non-neurological movement limitation; thus, default attribution to bilateral BPBI risks missing a serious central pathology. No standardized terminology or investigation framework currently addresses this phenotype. This review introduces bilateral upper-limb palsy of the newborn infant (BULPN) and proposes a three-category taxonomy separating 'true BULPN' (bilateral plexus-level palsy at birth) from mimics and acquired (postnatal-onset) palsy. True BULPN is most consistently reported in breech delivery and it is frequently asymmetric; published cohorts describe a high burden of concurrent phrenic nerve palsy. A localization-first diagnostic algorithm and time-anchored, severity-stratified management pathways are presented to support safer and more targeted clinical assessment and management, and reduce the risk of misdiagnosis.

> The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) offers a bio-psycho-social framework for understanding disability, yet its application in rehabilitation remains vulnerable to medical reductionism. This article argues that this tension reflects insufficient social-theoretical grounding of the Activity and Participation components, particularly concerning disabled persons’ agency. Through conceptual analysis, it integrates Rutger Claassen’s agency-based capability approach into the ICF. Within the proposed framework, Activity is linked to participatory agency: autonomous goal-setting and action within specific social practices. Participation is linked to navigational agency: the capacity to move between practices, negotiate competing demands, exit oppressive arrangements, and pursue structural reform. Distinguishing autonomy from freedom across internal capabilities and external opportunities provides an analytical basis for identifying constraints on agency. These distinctions inform a three-tier capability pathway comprising basic capabilities, participatory agency, and navigational agency. > Assistive and collaborative robots offer a promising solution for reducing human physical stress and exposure across a broad range of applications. The design and control of such robotic systems should account for humans needs, so as to assist their motion and activity as well as optimize their efficiency and performance throughout the considered tasks. In this respect, designing around the human means accounting for their musculoskeletal constraints, features, and limitations during the development of robotic mechanical systems and control algorithms, such as powered exoskeletons or cobots. This Chapter presents an overview of human-centered design and shared control techniques in robotics, including supporting examples and applications in the field of industrial teleoperation and mobility assistance. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This structured narrative review maps three literatures: medical education assessment instruments, clinical LLM benchmarks published from 2023 onwards, and general-domain methods for evaluating long-form generation. We examine six dimensions: problem representation, temporal synthesis, differential and management reasoning, counterfactual reasoning, calibrated uncertainty, and reasoning faithfulness. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23–1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26–1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups.

> OBJECTIVE: To present and validate a digital visual scale for evaluating mucosal wound repair after mandibular third molar extraction. The research seeks to establish a standard-based tool to improve communication in clinical practice and research by reducing subjectivity in postoperative assessments. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A digital image scale using four clinical inflammatory stages (Scores 0 to 3) of recovering oral mucosa of tooth extractions sites was construct. Employing electronic forms (n = 300) were sent to dentists to assess agreement with the consensus score, and construct validity in six tooth extraction mucosal wounds examined by specialists or not. Construct validation involved specialists who evaluated the scale's utility, graphic quality, and clinical significance via a 5-point Likert scale. There was a total of eighty-three responses for the agreement consensus, and sixty-seven for construct validation. RESULTS: The scale demonstrated a "fair" inter-rater agreement with a Fleiss' Kappa of 0.3018. > Vital pulp therapy (VPT) represents an increasingly relevant approach in contemporary endodontics, with the primary objective of maintaining pulp vitality and preserving the biological and functional integrity of the tooth. The preservation of vital pulp tissue is supported by its capacity to respond to microbial challenges, regulate inflammatory reactions, and initiate reparative responses after injury. The management of deep carious lesions has progressively favored minimally invasive procedures, including selective caries removal, indirect and direct pulp capping, partial pulpotomy, and full pulpotomy. The choice among these approaches should be guided by the extent of carious involvement, clinical findings, pulp status, and the anticipated healing capacity of the remaining tissue. Developments in calcium silicate-based and other bioceramic materials have expanded the therapeutic potential of VPT, particularly because of their favorable biological properties and sealing performance. Nevertheless, clinical outcomes are determined by a combination of factors rather than material selection alone. Pulpal and periapical diseases may present with overlapping clinical and radiographic features, while certain non-endodontic conditions can also mimic endodontic disease. These similarities may complicate diagnosis, particularly when symptoms are nonspecific, pulpal tests provide inconclusive results, or radiographic findings are limited. Therefore, endodontic diagnosis should be based on the integration of the patient’s history, clinical examination, pulpal and periapical tests, and radiographic findings. When necessary, advanced diagnostic methods, including cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and histopathological examination, can provide additional information. > Purpose: Delayed diagnosis in rare cancers can lead to disease progression, limited treatment options, and psychological distress, resulting in poorer quality of life and disability. We explored healthcare professionals' (HCPs) perceptions of diagnostic delay in rare cancers and options for patient support. Materials and methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 HCPs involved in rare cancer care. Interview topics covered diagnostic challenges, causes of delays, consequences for patients, and support options. Data were analyzed thematically. Results Three main themes emerged: (1) Time, intuition, and a safety-net fill the gap when signs are present, but not obvious . HCPs balance clinical intuition with safety-netting to avoid mis-, under-, or overdiagnosis when symptoms are vague, (2) Balancing speed and care in a fast-paced, complex diagnostic phase . Once cancer is suspected, the trajectory accelerates, yet systemic delays persist, and (3) Striving for precision: the paradox of reaching a diagnosis . While seizures and signs of raised intracranial pressure are common presenting features, isolated focal neurological deficits without systemic or meningeal symptoms are rare, resulting in diagnostic delay. We report an unusual case of thalamic tuberculoma presenting primarily with gait disturbance in a young child. A 2-year-old boy from Karachi, Pakistan, presented with inability to walk independently at 20 months age. On neurological examination, he had decreased power involving left side of body. MRI of the brain showed a ring-enhancing lesion in the right thalamus extending into the midbrain with surrounding vasogenic edema. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) showed a lipid/lactate peak, which supported an infectious granulomatous etiology; a presumptive diagnosis of tuberculoma was made based on imaging findings and household TB exposure. It follows a scientific progression from biodigital diagnosis and clinical decision-making to preventive care in pediatric dentistry; from the preservation of the pulp and natural dentition to periodontal and orthodontic treatment; and from digital prosthetic planning to implant-supported rehabilitation. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Philosophy in medicine is often described through application: philosophical concepts are brought to bear on illness, clinical relationships, ethics, or education. Yet this language can obscure forms of inquiry in which clinical experience also reshapes philosophical questions. This paper develops a conceptual account of reciprocal clinical philosophizing: a bidirectional, open-ended, and dialogical practice in which philosophical inquiry and clinical experience can each generate, constrain, and revise questions posed by the other. The argument does not claim that philosophy of medicine has generally been one-way; Canguilhem, phenomenological psychopathology, and contemporary phenomenology of illness already exemplify reciprocal inquiry. Rather, the "application model" is used as an ideal-typical contrast that names a recurrent pressure to make philosophy clinically legible through portable concepts, tools, or measurable outcomes. Three worked examples from Merleau-Ponty-language and expression, medical objectification, and intersubjectivity-show how reciprocity can operate. In each, philosophy unsettles a clinical category while clinical realities, including institutional asymmetr...

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Foundation models are routinely fine-tuned for use in particular domains, yet safety assessments are typically conducted only on base models, implicitly assuming that safety properties persist through downstream adaptation. To test this assumption, we evaluate an ecologically valid sample of fine-tuned models for medical and legal applications. We compare each with their respective base models to assess changes in general-purpose and domain specific safety behavior from fine-tuning. We find that benign fine-tuning induces large, heterogeneous, and often contradictory changes in measured safety: models frequently improve on some instruments while degrading on others, with substantial disagreement across evaluations. We show that safety performance changes unpredictably under realistic downstream adaptation. Our results indicate that models must be evaluated after modification to accurately measure risk. Given that many AI governance proposals rely on base model evaluations, this casts doubt on their ability to effectively manage risk. At the same time, allocating all responsibility to actors that fine-tune and deploy models, risks placing undue burden on the least resourced and powe...

> Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh tuntutan akademik mahasiswa keperawatan yang dapat berkaitan dengan motivasi belajar dan stres akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui hubungan motivasi belajar dengan tingkat stres akademik pada mahasiswa Keperawatan Semester VI Universitas Yatsi Madani. Penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan desain deskriptif korelasional dan pendekatan cross-sectional. Populasi berjumlah 193 mahasiswa dengan sampel 130 responden yang dipilih menggunakan proportional stratified random sampling. Instrumen penelitian berupa kuesioner motivasi belajar dan Educational Stress Scale for Adolescents (ESSA). Analisis data meliputi analisis univariat dan bivariat menggunakan uji Chi-Square. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan motivasi belajar sebagian besar berada pada kategori sedang sebanyak 61 responden (46,9%) dan stres akademik kategori sedang sebanyak 62 responden (47,7%). Uji Chi-Square menghasilkan p-value = 0,001 (p < 0,05). Kesimpulannya, terdapat hubungan yang signifikan antara motivasi belajar dan tingkat stres akademik pada mahasiswa Keperawatan Semester VI Universitas Yatsi Madani.

However, research remains largely focused on adoption and current-oriented practices such as short‑term usage and immediate convenience, offering limited insight into how DFS can foster users’ future financial lives and financial well-being, especially for young people who are digitally adept but financially precarious. Financial well‑being, understood as a sense of security and freedom in meeting present and future financial needs, includes both hedonic, and eudaimonic, toward meaningful goals. It is particularly challenging in youth-focused DFS. Drawing on activity theory, we conceptualise financial well-being as an evolving, practice-based activity rather than a static outcome state and investigate how DFS can be effectively leveraged to cultivate young users’ financial well-being. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Stigmatisation can undermine participation, belonging and well-being in higher education. This study examined how students represent stigmatisation and connect it to diversity, inclusion and perceived institutional responsibility. Grounded in social representations theory, it used a cross-sectional qualitative textual design. A non-probabilistic snowball sample of 519 students from one Spanish university completed an online free-association task based on the Grid Elaboration Method, providing four words and brief explanations in response to “stigmatisation”. Spanish-language responses were analysed in IRaMuTeQ using similarity analysis and descending hierarchical cluster analysis (Reinert method). Seven classes formed two broader branches. The first constructed stigmatisation as categorisation and discrimination affecting LGBTQ+ people, migrants, and people with mental health conditions or functional diversity, with perceived consequences including emotional suffering and academic harm. The second connected stigmatisation to unmet support needs, rigid assessment practices and insufficient institutional responsiveness. By mapping spontaneous associations across multiple forms of dif...

> Background: While the electronic health records (EHR) is a critical tool for clinical care in academic medical centers, there is a gap in the literature regarding utilization of EHRs for teaching and learning in residency training, outside of descriptions on EHR training or use for quality improvement projects. The research question for this scoping review is: How is the EHR purposefully used in educational interventions for teaching and learning in graduate medical education? Methods We searched all publications in PubMed, SCOPUS, CINAHL, ERIC, Cochrane and MedEdPORTAL databases from 2010 to 2022 that met our search criteria and MeSH terms. Using Arksey and O'Malley's framework, the abstracts were reviewed by three team members, and the full text was reviewed by all authors using a standardized data extraction sheet. Results Of the 2431 records, 19 met inclusion criteria and were reviewed in full. All studies were set in North America, 79% at teaching hospitals, and 42% in Internal Medicine programs. The EHR was used purposefully to improve learning in sepsis, diabetes, asthma, critical care, post- and peri-operative care, and it was used to provide feedback about clinical perform...

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Humans are increasingly expected to interact with AI systems that observe and make inferences about them - but do these systems actually work? A standard approach to answering this question is AI auditing. Conducting an AI audit requires identifying how a system behaves (i.e., determining what types of inputs to audit it with and then observing and documenting actual system behavior) and contrasting that with how a system should behave (i.e., determining what the nominal outputs of a system should look like). We argue that this is best done through a contextual audit, which we introduce as a method for auditing measurements within the context of the practices that produce them. We show how contextual auditing enables the interrogation of assumptions implicit in the audit process and allows auditors to be explicit about what serves as ground truth, which we define as verifiable measurements about the real world against which systems are evaluated. We outline how the concept of symmetry from science and technology studies can enable audits when ground truth is unknown, unknowable, or contested. Finally, to demonstrate how contextual and symmetric audits can be conducted in practice,...

> BACKGROUND: The current financing model for US dental education is increasingly misaligned with the goals of sustainability, equity, and workforce design. Tuition has risen substantially over time, educational debt among dental graduates remains high, and evidence suggests that price affects enrollment decisions and student diversity. High debt may also constrain career choice, reducing graduates' flexibility to pursue academic, hospital-based, public-serving, and safety-net careers. At the same time, major reform reports across the past century have repeatedly argued that dental education must periodically redesign its structure, financing, and institutional role in response to changing social needs and health systems. > The modernization of medical education requires the introduction of innovative pedagogical approaches that strengthen students' clinical reasoning, practical competence, and professional decision-making. Urology is a clinical discipline in which theoretical knowledge must be closely integrated with diagnostic and procedural skills. This thesis examines the potential of clinical case-based simulation and competency-oriented education in improving the quality of urology teaching. A narrative analysis of scientific literature on simulation-based learning, clinical reasoning, and medical education was conducted. Particular attention was given to the application of simulated clinical scenarios involving urinary retention, renal colic, hematuria, and urinary tract infections. The analysis suggests that structured clinical simulations, combined with objective assessment and timely feedback, can provide a more interactive educational environment and facilitate the development of practical competencies. The proposed methodological approach emphasizes gradual progression from theoretical knowledge to simulated clinical decision-making and supervised patient care.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract Competency-based surgical education requires objective, scalable assessment of technical skill, yet existing rating scales are subjective. Objective performance indicators (OPIs) derived from console kinematics, offer a solution; however, they lack a validated scoring framework. We developed and externally validated an OPI-based scoring system from robotic transabdominal preperitoneal inguinal hernia repairs performed by 6 attendings and 41 trainees at an academic center (2023–2026). Nineteen OPIs across four tasks were grouped into eight domains, reduced by principal component analysis, and integrated into task-specific 0–100 composite scores via ridge logistic regression. Among 2588 tasks from 392 cases, cross-validated AUCs for attending-trainee discrimination were 0.62–0.74, and composite scores increased from postgraduate year 2 to attending (Spearman ρ, 0.94–1.00; P ≤ 0.005). In an independent external cohort (84 observations, 21 cases), the overall AUC was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.69–0.93). This framework enables objective technical skills assessment in robotic hernia repair.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Firms frequently engage in impression management to protect their reputations in times of crises that bring higher stakeholder scrutiny. This study investigates firms’ deployment of visual impression management tactics, both overt and subliminal, in response to an industry scandal – the Deepwater Horizon oil spill. Leveraging digital archive querying and image processing, we examined monthly visual snapshots of website homepages for 1,971 publicly traded firms from May 2007 to April 2013 and analyzed the pixel content of over 118,038 images using a red–green–blue (RGB) color model. Results reveal that the exogenous shock of the Deepwater Horizon oil spill caused oil and gas companies to increase their website green color prevalence relative to control firms. Notably, firms with poor environmental reputations were more inclined to adopt subliminal strategies by enhancing the green color on their websites. This work contributes to our understanding of selective mimeticism and the subtle art of environmental signaling in the face of reputational challenges, providing valuable insights for external stakeholders concerned with greenwashing and digital impression management.

This review aims to highlight the synergistic induction of ferroptosis through nanomedicine, immunotherapy, and targeted therapeutic agents for the treatment of breast and gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies. Nanotechnology‐based targeted delivery systems enhance the delivery of ferroptosis‐inducing agents to cancer cells while minimizing the toxicity of these agents to healthy cells.   - **negative_keywords** : paediatric

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) are typically scored by a single examiner per station, exposing results to hard-to-audit examiner variability. We developed the Rater-Aware Verification Network (RAVEN), a multimodal Artificial Intelligence (AI) system fusing egocentric video, examiner verbalisations and marks, and virtual reality (VR) action logs as an examiner-conditioned second marker for paediatric OSCEs (retrospective evaluation; 120 students, 442 ratings, eight domains). A confidence-gated hybrid improved agreement with leave-one-examiner-out consensus on the pass/fail decision (AC1: +6.2 percentage points; p = 0.0004) and domain scores (mean AC2: +3.0 points, five of eight significant), with the largest gains on borderline-fail cases (+16.3 points of concordance with consensus). Comparing AI-inferred, rubric-specified, and examiner-articulated criteria revealed implicit practices absent from marking guidelines. Agreement is measured against a panel-derived reference rather than an external ground truth; the system is intended as an audit and flagging aid for human adjudication rather than an autonomous decision-maker.

The broad differential diagnosis and frequent absence of an identifiable cause can lead to repeated investigations, delayed treatment and unnecessary surgery. This review provides a practical overview of the assessment and management of CSCP, based on contemporary American Urological Association and European Association of Urology guidance, and the current literature. We describe a structured approach to history, examination and investigation, highlighting important red flags and common causes, including post‐vasectomy pain syndrome, chronic epididymitis, neuropathic pain, pelvic floor dysfunction, referred pain and malignancy. Management should begin with conservative, multidisciplinary treatment tailored to the underlying pain mechanism. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Introduction Student-assisted, -run or -led health clinics (SLCs) are increasingly common worldwide, but student outcomes remain under-evaluated, with existing work focused narrowly on clinical and/or academic outcomes. Methods This study presents the findings of an evaluation of the impact of a student-assisted clinic in New Zealand, on participating students subjective wellbeing, assessed using the Satisfaction with Life Scale (SWLS), as well as on a range of programme-related intermediate outcomes theorised to support wellbeing, including leadership, communication, and clinical capability. Students undertaking placements at the clinic were surveyed at three time points: at the start, the end, and at six months post-placement. Results Participating students maintained levels of self-reported wellbeing over placement periods while significantly improving leadership, purpose, cultural connection, and clinical capability. Income and sleep were shown to be key factors related to SWLS scores. Discussion Student-related outcomes from SLCs may extend beyond clinical care and academic performance, highlighting the value of a more holistic approach to SLC evaluation.

> How can the ways we produce and value knowledge generate racial inequities in oral health? This article presents an investigation of this new, epistemic determinant of oral health, analysing how Black patients may have their reports, experiences and concerns systematically discounted during dental care. Drawing on the epistemic injustice theory, we develop a philosophical-conceptual framework, informed by a hermeneutics-guided, narrative review of the literature, to posit the epistemic mechanisms underpinning this phenomenon. According to our conceptual framework, biomedically-oriented and whiteness-influenced dental education and the epistemically unequal character of health systems and training intertwine, generating a pattern of systematically compounded discredibility by dental staff towards Black patients. The model compares wavelengths of 810, 850, and 900 nm and evaluates the effects of optical power, beam radius, and a 180 s exposure period. Following a quality-of-care assessment in two Ugandan hospitals, the collaboration identified four priority areas: paediatric emergency care, neonatology, child neurology with a focus on epilepsy, and child rights. The adaptation comprised translation of the interface into Uzbek, nosological revision of the scenario library, alignment of diagnostic and treatment algorithms with national clinical protocols, and technical modification of the software. The resulting set comprises 36 classes (108 academic hours) and 136 clinical scenarios distributed across basic, core and advanced modules. It was implemented with 285 students in their 3rd to 6th years of study. In all modules, task performance improved significantly from the first to the final class (p<0.001). > The integration of innovative educational technologies into medical education has become an essential component of improving the quality of professional training. Urology requires students to acquire theoretical knowledge, clinical reasoning abilities, and practical procedural skills. Traditional teaching methods may not always provide sufficient opportunities for repeated practice and objective assessment. This thesis examines the educational significance of interactive simulation, digital learning platforms, and competency-based assessment in undergraduate urology education. Particular attention is given to urinary catheterization training, virtual clinical scenarios, and structured practical examinations. Based on a narrative analysis of published scientific literature, an integrated teaching model is proposed that combines theoretical preparation, simulation-based exercises, formative feedback, and supervised clinical practice. The proposed approach may improve the organization of practical training, support independent learning, and promote patient safety.

> Objective Guided by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) as a conceptual framework, this study explored medical students’ use of large language models (LLMs) in graduation thesis writing, focusing on application patterns, perceptions, and potential risks. Methods A comparative cross-sectional questionnaire survey using convenience sampling was conducted among medical graduates from medical schools in China in 2024 and 2025. The self-designed 25-item questionnaire included five-point Likert items on perceived advantages and disadvantages of LLMs. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's α , exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was performed, and univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with LLMs use. Results A total of 341 valid questionnaires were collected. Overall, 54.25% (185/341) of respondents reported using LLMs in graduation thesis writing, with use reported by 27.37% (52/190) in 2024 and 88.08% (133/151) in 2025. ChatGPT was the most frequently used platform in 2024 (82.69%, 43/52), whereas Deepseek was the most frequently used platform in 2025 (88.72%, 118/133). > Introduction Vestibulodynia (VBD) is a common chronic pelvic pain condition with heterogeneous clinical presentation, including subtypes distinguished by the presence (VBD-central; VBD-c) or absence (VBD-peripheral; VBD-p) of comorbid pain conditions. Despite frequent prescribing of topical therapies such as lidocaine/estradiol and centrally-acting agents such as tricyclic antidepressants, high-quality evidence for efficacy, alone or in combination, remains limited. This study evaluated effects of peripheral, central, and combined pharmacologic treatments for two VBD subtypes and whether treatment response varied by subtype.Patients and Methods We conducted a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03844412) at two academic medical centers. Women aged 18–50 with clinician-confirmed VBD were randomized to one of four treatment arms: 1) topical 5% lidocaine + 0.05% estradiol vaginal cream and placebo pill, 2) oral nortriptyline pill and placebo cream, 3) combined active pill and cream, or 4) double placebo for 16 weeks. In this Review, we survey the principal AI architectures that currently support spinal imaging, including convolutional neural networks, object detectors, and hybrid models, and we assess their reported performance for osteoporotic, traumatic, and pathological vertebral fractures. Our synthesis indicates that AI can achieve high diagnostic accuracy in controlled, often single-centre retrospective settings, but its performance consistently declines for mild fractures, degenerated spines, and postoperative anatomy. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Sleep quality plays a vital role in maintaining overall health and psychological well-being. However, sleep disturbances are increasingly prevalent among university students due to academic stress, irregular sleep schedules, and lifestyle factors. This study aimed to examine the serial mediating roles of physical pain intensity and mental well-being in the relationship between problematic internet use (PIU) and sleep quality. The sample consisted of 410 Turkish university students (295 females, 72.0%; 115 males, 28.0%) reflecting the gender distribution of health-related academic programs. Serial mediation analysis using the PROCESS macro (Model 6) was conducted. The findings revealed that PIU was positively associated with poorer sleep quality, with a significant serial indirect effect through physical pain intensity and mental well-being. These results highlight the intertwined physical and psychological mechanisms underlying sleep disturbances among university students.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disease that primarily affects the motor system. A minority of cases are associated with a genetic variant. Variants in C9orf72, SOD1, TARDBP, and FUS are the most common. Compared with other forms of ALS, ALS presenting with FUS variants is relatively aggressive. However, phenotypic heterogeneity has been reported. We describe two cases of ALS with rare FUS variants with contrasting clinical courses. These cases highlight the importance of the different factors that influence ALS phenotypic presentation and the challenges of variant interpretation in ALS, as outlined in the ACMG Guidelines. It is essential to recognise specific genotype-phenotype relationships and environmental factors that could alter the clinical course of the disease and affect therapeutic agent selection.

This review aims to summarize the epidemiological characteristics and assessment methods of osteoporosis in AIS, with a primary focus on elucidating how it contributes to curve progression by influencing the spine’s mechanical properties. Pri digitalni radiografiji lahko elektronsko zaslanjanje oz. obrezovanje slike naknadno zmanjša prikazano slikovno polje in s tem prikrije dejansko velikost obsevanega področja. Namen: Namen magistrskega dela je bil oceniti učinkovitost nastavitve primarnega slikovnega polja pri izbranih rentgenskih preiskavah v splošni radiološki diagnostiki. Želeli smo ugotoviti pogostost neustreznega zaslanjanja, oceniti razlike med primarno eksponiranim in elektronsko zaslonjenim slikovnim poljem ter primerjati vrednosti produkta doze in površine (DAP) in ocenjenega nepotrebnega DAP med dobro in slabo zaslonjenimi rentgenogrami. Metode dela: Izvedli smo retrospektivno raziskavo, v katero smo vključili 603 rentgenograme vratne, torakalne in ledvene hrbtenice, rame ter kolka. > The role of isometric plantar flexion (PF) strength in sprinting and jumping is unclear and, in part, may be due to methodological issues with isometric dynamometry leading to inaccurate measures of PF strength. In addition, the relationship, and thus functional relevance, of isometric PF strength with PF kinetics during these athletic tasks remains unknown. The aim of this study was to assess the interrelationships of isometric PF strength, task-specific sprint and jump PF kinetics and overall performance during jumps and sprint acceleration. Three-dimensional kinematics and ground reaction forces were recorded in 38 healthy individuals of varying athletic ability (18 females; height 1.75 ± 0.09 m; Mass: 70.9 ± 10.0 kg, Age 23 ± 3 years) during: standing isometric PF dynamometry, countermovement jumps (CMJ), drop jumps (DJ) and sprints. Isometric PF strength and sprint/jump PF kinetics were both assessed via inverse dynamics. Sprint speed, CMJ height and DJ reactive strength index defined task performances. Specific sprint and jump PF kinetics showed moderate-large correlations to task performances in 7 out of 9 relationships with peak positive power explaining 19-50% of the varia...

> Abstract The dynamics of calcium ions (Ca 2+ ) in skeletal muscles link electrochemical activation and contractile force generation. Recent experimental data suggest that store-operated Ca 2+ entry (SOCE), the process of extracellular Ca 2+ influx upon depletion of Ca 2+ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR), helps delay the onset of muscle fatigue during exercise. We hypothesize that SOCE regulates force generation during prolonged muscle activity by allowing for sustained Ca 2+ release from the SR. We test this hypothesis with a quantitative biophysical model that simulates the biochemical events of muscle contraction, from depolarization at the T-tubules to Ca 2+ release from the SR to Ca 2+ binding and force generation throughout the myoplasm. We also consider the balance between Ca 2+ removal from the myoplasm and SOCE through the T-tubule membrane, along with mitochondrial uptake of free Ca 2+ and phosphate. We use the model to test the effects of SOCE inhibition on force production. The magnitude of myoplasmic Ca 2+ and force are lower in SOCE knockout cells, especially when SOCE reduction is combined with impaired uptake of phosphate by mitochondria. Case A 17-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis in the setting of a heterozygous SPINK1 N34S (c.101A > G; p.Asn34Ser) variant, presented with acute-on-chronic abdominal pain severe enough to require escalating opioid therapy; imaging demonstrated calcifications, edema, and peripancreatic fluid collections. This research guided review integrates physiological, transcriptomic, metabolomics, and computational evidence to translate current knowledge of FLVs-associated drought responses in purple barley into future research directions. It is a multifactorial disorder of persistent or recurrent pelvic pain lasting at least three to six months, associated with impaired physical, psychological, sexual and social functioning. Various classifications have been proposed to describe the diverse phenotypic presentations, as well as the frequent overlap of pain conditions and comorbidities. A common classification used by urologists is interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) in women and chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) in men. The European Association of Urology (EAU) distinguishes secondary CPPS, in which identifiable pathology such as Hunner-lesion interstitial cystitis, chronic bacterial prostatitis or endometriosis is present, from primary CPPS, which occurs without demonstrable pathology. > Analgesic nephropathy (AN) remains a critical yet under-recognized cause of chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis and progressive renal injury in contemporary internal medicine. While historically associated with phenacetin abuse, the clinical landscape in 2026 is driven by chronic, high-dose combination regimens of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and acetaminophen (paracetamol), often augmented by caffeine or codeine. This narrative review addresses three primary objectives: summarizing current epidemiological trends and risk factors, highlighting the synergistic nephrotoxicity of combination analgesics and host hemodynamic vulnerabilities; detailing the dual-pathway pathophysiological mechanisms that cause medullary vasoganglion ischemic injury and toxic metabolite-induced oxidative stress, progressing to renal papillary necrosis (RPN) and chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis (CIN); and presenting a practical, ward-based action plan for internists encompassing targeted admission medication reconciliation, protection of renal autoregulation, safe inpatient multimodal pain protocols, and patient education. > Background: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) frequently develop cardiogenic pulmonary edema and associated respiratory muscle weakness, reduced chest expansion, increased dyspnea and reduced quality of life. Inspiratory muscle training (IMT) may help improve respiratory mechanics, oxygenation and patient reported outcomes in this population. Context and Purpose of Study: To examine the effectiveness of supervised IMT in CKD patients with cardiogenic pulmonary edema using chest expansion, mMRC dyspnea, and SpO₂. Results: The study showed significant improvements in all measured outcomes following the intervention. The average mMRC dyspnea score was reduced from 3.60 ± 0.55 to 1.00 ± 0.00 (p < 0.001), while mean SpO₂ increased from 91.80 ± 1.30% to 98.00 ± 1.00% (p = 0.001). Chest expansion also improved in all participants, indicating enhanced respiratory function. Overall, these findings demonstrate meaningful enhancements in respiratory function and clinical status. Conclusion: The study found that IMT helped reduce dyspnea and improve oxygenation and chest expansion in CKD patients with cardiogenic pulmonary edema. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Ergonomics is inherently based on disciplinary integration: a compulsory condition to lead the systemic understanding and improvement of real-world complexities like the ones of Human-Robot Interactions (HRIs). Accordingly, this chapter ponders the contributions of diverse disciplines to the study of human factors alongside their synergies with the multi-faceted area of robotics. Key examples are presented, considering problems requiring approaches like bio-inspired soft robotics, value-sensitive design, interactions and affective features, and neuroergonomics in HRI. The implications about education on HRI ergonomics are also pondered. Overall, this chapter remarks how diverse backgrounds can lead to contributions to the human-centered design and assessment of robots if the experts, regardless of disciplinary boundaries, just focus on learning novel perspectives and methods to solve the problems occurring in Human-Robot Systems.

### Anchor‐Free Capsular Augmentation Using the Reflected Head of the Rectus Femoris in Hip Arthroscopy

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **negative_keywords** : postoperative

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Capsular integrity is a key factor in hip stability after arthroscopic procedures. Inadequate capsular closure may contribute to postoperative microinstability, persistent pain, and suboptimal outcomes, particularly in patients undergoing extensive capsulotomy or procedures affecting proximal capsular tissue. Most capsular augmentation techniques using the reflected head of the rectus femoris rely on suture anchors for tendon fixation. This technical note describes an anchor-free capsular augmentation technique using the reflected head of the rectus femoris. A capsule-tendon-capsule suture construct is created using a suture-passing device, allowing simultaneous capsular closure and reinforcement without additional implants. The technique is simple, reproducible, and cost-effective and preserves the dynamic stabilizing role of the rectus femoris while maintaining physiologic capsular excursion.

We report an exceptionally rare case of adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS) diagnosed after 12 years of radiological follow-up of a pure GGO initially detected at 14 years of age. A 26-year-old never-smoker was referred to our department because of gradual enlargement of a pure GGO in the right upper lobe. The lesion had been incidentally detected during preoperative evaluation for dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans of the left upper arm at 14 years of age. Because primary lung adenocarcinoma was strongly suspected, the patient underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic extended right posterior segmentectomy (S2). Histopathological examination demonstrated lepidic proliferation of atypical pneumocytes without stromal invasion, confirming AIS (pTisN0M0, Stage 0). > Background Bartholin gland abscess and perianal abscess are common suppurative infections involving anatomically adjacent regions of the female perineum. Because both conditions may present with localized pain and swelling, distinguishing their respective origins and determining the extent of infection can be challenging. The concomitant occurrence of these two abscesses is uncommon, and its diagnostic and therapeutic considerations remain poorly characterized. We report a rare case of concomitant Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses and describe the diagnostic process and multidisciplinary surgical management. Case presentation An 18-year-old woman presented with progressive perineal and perianal pain and swelling. Pelvic computed tomography demonstrated abscess formation involving the perianal and left perineal soft tissues, and a possible communication between the two lesions was initially suspected. Emergency surgery was performed. The perianal abscess was incised and drained, and an infected anal gland was identified and excised, with bridge drainage established between the drainage incisions. > Background Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) is an ultrarare autosomal dominant disorder caused by ACVR1 gene mutations, leading to dysregulated bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling. It is characterized by congenital great toe malformations and progressive, trauma-induced heterotopic ossification (HO). Misdiagnosis is common, and invasive procedures can exacerbate HO. Current management focuses on flare-up control and trauma prevention. Case presentation A 12-year-old Asian boy presented with a left femoral fracture. His history included developmental delay, and HO formation after a prior forearm fracture surgery and other traumas, resulting in progressively limited joint mobility. Physical examination revealed bilateral hallux valgus and multiple hard masses. Imaging confirmed extensive HO. To avoid surgery-induced ossification, closed reduction and casting were performed, alongside comprehensive trauma prophylaxis education and follow-up planning. Conclusion This case highlights the critical importance of early recognition of FOP, with particular attention to distinctive great toe abnormalities, to prevent harmful interventions. Methods GH-pAb (hereinafter XON7) were generated by immunization of double-knockout pigs with human tumor cells. Antigen specificity of XON7 was assessed using a human proteome array and validated by ELISA. Anti-tumor mechanisms were evaluated in vitro on 2D or 3D-cultures. Efficacy was tested in vivo in cell or patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX), in chicken chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model, and in orthotopic/metastatic triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) models. Results XON7 demonstrated tumor-restricted binding across tissue microarrays without detectable staining in matched normal tissues. > As tecnologias digitais ampliaram as possibilidades de acompanhamento pós-operatório, mas sua incorporação ao cuidado biopsicossocial permanece heterogênea. A seleção seguiu critérios previamente definidos e o PRISMA 2020, resultando em 46 estudos. O risco de viés foi avaliado pelo RoB 2 nos 39 ensaios randomizados e por instrumentos do Joanna Briggs Institute nos sete estudos não randomizados. Predominaram aplicativos móveis, telemonitoramento, telerreabilitação, dispositivos vestíveis e soluções de inteligência artificial. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

As one of the highest-spend and highest-variation categories in healthcare, MSK represents one of the largest remaining opportunities to meaningfully reduce total cost of care and enhance patient outcomes. Orthopaedic and spine surgeons (specialists) stand at a critical inflection point: They can either lead the redesign of MSK care delivery across the entire patient journey or be relegated to procedural technicians within systems designed by others. Recent federal policy signals, including CMS’ TEAM, ACCESS, and Ambulatory Specialty Care models, make it clear that specialty-driven accountability is no longer optional. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Cage material selection in spinal fusion requires a trade-off among biological fixation, mechanical compatibility, subsidence resistance, and postoperative imaging. This structured narrative review compares titanium and polyetheretherketone (PEEK) cages across seven domains: osseointegration, modulus matching, endplate load transfer, surface biofunctionality, imaging, additive manufacturing and personalization, and geometry-guided architecture. Peer-reviewed literature indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was considered from database inception through May 2026, with emphasis on comparative clinical studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and mechanistic studies directly relevant to cage design. However, for some patients with typical clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings consistent with DAVF, the initial angiography may fail to detect the lesion. Straight Leg Raise Test was negative bilaterally, suggesting absence of nerve root involvement. However, Compression Overload Test was strongly positive, indicating mechanical disc pathology. Magnetic resonance imaging confirmed L5-S1 left paracentral disc herniation (protrusion type) with no neural compression. This case illustrates the diagnostic utility of Compression Overload Test in detecting lumbar disc herniation when traditional neurodynamic tests are negative, consistent with recent validation research showing 92% sensitivity for Compression Overload Test versus 28% for Straight Leg Raise Test. The patient received conservative chiropractic management with significant symptomatic improvement. Integration of Compression Overload Test into clinical examination protocols may enhance diagnostic accuracy in non-radicular low back pain presentations.

Materials and Methods A 40-year-old male presented with a three-year history of progressive sensory ataxia, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, visual disturbance, and slurred speech, with chronic dietary cassava intake. Examination revealed wide-based ataxic gait, and positive Romberg's sign; audiometry confirmed bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. The condition was diagnosed as Dushivisha Janya Vatavyadhi (Anukta Vatavyadhi), with vitiation of Prana, Udana, and Vyana Vata and progressive Dhatukshaya. Chronic cassava ingestion was considered Dushivisha, precipitating Agnimandya, Ama formation, and Srotodushti. Management included Koshtashodhana, Sarvanga Abhyanga, Nasya with Lashunaksheerapaka, Shashtika Shali Pinda Sweda, and Mustadi Rajayapana Basti, with supportive Shamana Aushadhis. Results: notable improvement in speech clarity and vision, with modest gain in tinnitus and gait. Markedly r...

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract Aging is a complex biological process influenced by chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysregulation, collectively termed inflammaging. The HEBE (Healthy aging versus inflamm-aging: the role of physical Exercise in modulating the Biomarkers of age-associated and Environmentally determined chronic diseases) project developed and implemented a consortium-driven, cost-effective methodological framework for biomarker profiling aimed at capturing these mechanisms and their modulation by lifestyle interventions, particularly physical exercise. This framework integrates interdisciplinary expertise and high-throughput analytical strategies to guide biomarker selection while balancing physiological relevance, analytical feasibility, and cost-effectiveness. The framework was applied within a large multidisciplinary consortium structured across multiple research lines (RLs), each addressing specific domains of inflammaging-related conditions, including obesity, cancer, frailty, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, neuroinflammation, psychological stress, autoimmune disorders, and fertility.
